summary: Nopone lookout tower, Hall County, Georgia: the only source found is a December 1955 newspaper account of a rescue on the tower. No build date or fate found.

events.note: Mary Etta Evans, a member of the Hall County Forest Fire Protective Association, went to her station at the tower; she became ill and collapsed. Gainesville firefighters reached her, and she was brought down in a rescue harness

evidence.supports: went to her station at the Nopone tower, December 1955
evidence.quote: went to her station at Nopone lookout tower north of Gainesville yesterday morning.
She is Mrs. Mary Etta Evans

evidence.supports: member of the Hall County Forest Fire Protective Association
evidence.quote: a member of the Hall County Forest Fire Protective Association

evidence.supports: collapsed and stayed on the tower for several hours before rescue
evidence.quote: collapsed and remained several hours in freezing weather on a forest fire lookout tower before being rescued

evidence.supports: strong winds and icy ladder steps made reaching her difficult; firemen reached her
evidence.quote: After considerable difficulty reaching the top of the tower because of strong winds and icy ladder steps, firemen reached her.

evidence.supports: Gainesville Fire Department called to the scene
evidence.quote: Several hours later the Gainesville Fire Department was called to the scene.

evidence.supports: brought down in a rescue harness with tie lines
evidence.quote: She was brought down in a wind tossed Davis rescue harness with the help of tie lines.

corrections.why: The cited page describes only the 1955 rescue and says nothing about the tower's condition. No source I read supports 'ruins'.

sources.title: Nopone - Forest Lookouts
sources.publisher: Eastern US Forest Lookouts (quoting The Macon News, December 10, 1955)

notes_for_editor: Only one historical source (a 1955 newspaper account quoted on the Eastern US page). No build date, design, agency or fate found. Two web searches returned nothing on the tower. They did show Nopone Road in Gainesville (ZIP 30506) and the North Hall Community Center and Park at 4175 Nopone Road; no source ties the road or park to the tower site, so they are not used. Possible lead for Hall County Library local history or Georgia Forestry Commission records. The status 'ruins' in the record has no support in the sources read; see correction. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the full 1955 text on the Eastern US page was checked. It does not say the firefighters lowered her, so the story now says they reached her and she was brought down in a harness. Elevation units: the TN Landforms list does not label them; 1,480 is read as feet, because the same list gives Brasstown Lookout Tower as 4,735 and Brasstown Bald, Georgia's highest point, is about 4,784 feet.
